# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**To:** CommunityCare — Member Appeals
Use the appeal address printed on my denial letter, or the address given when calling the number on the back of my insurance card.

**From:**
Skyler Foster
Member ID: W944120051
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

---

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-13**
**Reference number:** POC-DA7FAA7DB4-93242
**Member:** Skyler Foster — **Member ID:** W944120051
**Denied service:** Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
**Plan:** CommunityCare (Commercial/ACA), Oklahoma
**Governing policy cited in this appeal:** *2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines*, https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization for a total hip replacement (CPT 27130), which CommunityCare denied on 2026-08-13. The notice states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery.

I am writing because the imaging in my chart matches the kind of findings the plan's own guidelines describe, and because my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this surgery is needed. Below I have lined up the plan's published language with what my records actually say.

## The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

The *2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines* state:

> "THA may be considered medically necessary as indicated in either sections 1 or 2:"

and

> "Persistent pain and documented loss of function with radiographic evidence of disease from any of the following:"

Both of these sentences end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that I have not been provided in full. I am responding to the criteria language available to me, and I ask the plan to identify in writing the specific criteria it applied to my request.

**1. My imaging shows the definitive findings the policy describes, not just a general label.**

The guidelines state:

> "Radiographic findings show evidence of advanced arthritic changes, described as Tönnis grade 2 or 3 [see Grading Appendix] or described as X-rays showing advanced changes (e.g., severe narrowing, bone-on-bone compartment collapse, subchondral sclerosis or cysts, osteophyte formation and/or bony deformity etc.)"

and:

> "X-rays described only as showing 'severe', 'advanced' or 'end-stage' arthritis require more definitive descriptions as stated above (weightbearing X-rays are not required)"

My records are not limited to a general label. My weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph of 2026-06-08 reports the joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes. Narrowing, subchondral sclerosis and osteophyte formation are the specific descriptors the policy itself lists. This is exactly the "more definitive description" the guideline asks for, and it is the type of study the guideline contemplates — the policy also notes:

> "NOTE: MRI should not be the primary radiographic test used to determine the presence or severity of arthritic changes in the joint."

My determination rests on a plain radiograph, not an MRI. Since the denial rests on the imaging, I ask the reviewer to compare the 2026-06-08 radiograph report directly against the descriptive language quoted above.

**2. I have symptoms and documented loss of function — I am not an imaging-only case.**

The guidelines state:

> "There is no medical necessity to perform THA in individuals with severe radiological disease and no symptoms, except in the case of malignancy."

and:

> "There is persistent pain and documented loss of function for at least 12 weeks and includes all the following"

I have had 9 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest. My records document that I walk with a cane, that I am limited to one block, and that I cannot put on my shoes unassisted. That is well beyond the 12 weeks the policy states, and it is documented loss of function, not an incidental x-ray finding.

**3. My physical exam findings match the policy's list.**

The guidelines state:

> "Physical exam (PE) demonstrates findings of hip pathology as evidence by one or more of the following (PE is not required if bone-on-bone narrowing is present on X-ray):"

and include among those findings:

> "Painful, limited range of motion or antalgic gait"

My exam documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. That matches the finding quoted directly above.

**4. I completed more than the conservative care the policy requires.**

The guidelines state:

> "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least two of the following (1–3,5):"

Two of the listed options are:

> "Protected weight-bearing with cane, walker, or crutches"

> "Physician supervised exercise program (including home exercise program)"

My records show both. I completed supervised physical therapy focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait — 16 visits over 16 weeks, from 2026-03-11 to 2026-07-01, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I also ambulate with a cane. In addition, I took NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief. My 16 weeks of therapy exceeds the 12 weeks the policy states. The guidelines also ask the reviewer to consider:

> "Type and duration of non-operative management modalities"

The type and duration are both in the chart, as set out above.

**5. The injection timing and my medical optimization.**

The guidelines state:

> "No corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of surgery (1,7–9)"

My corticosteroid injection was on 2026-05-19 and gave only 3 weeks of partial relief. That date is already more than 12 weeks in the past, and my surgery is not yet scheduled because of this denial. My planned surgery date is [surgery date, once scheduled], which is more than 12 weeks after the injection.

The guidelines also state:

> "Individual is medically stable and optimized for surgery, and any treatable comorbidities are adequately medically managed such as diabetes, nicotine addiction, or an excessively high body mass index (BMI)."

My records document no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

## Please send me the criteria that were applied

The plan, not I, holds the clinical review criteria used to decide my case. I am asking CommunityCare to provide me, in writing, a complete copy of the specific criteria applied to this request, including the individual line items the reviewer found unmet and the reason the 2026-06-08 radiograph findings were considered insufficient. I understand CommunityCare posts an InterQual viewer that does not require a login, and that a move to MCG was announced on or after 2026-08-01. Please tell me which criteria set was in effect and applied on my decision date of 2026-08-13, and provide the credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination.

## Closing request

I am asking CommunityCare to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-13 (reference POC-DA7FAA7DB4-93242) and authorize CPT 27130. The plan's guidelines call for radiographic evidence described in definitive terms, symptoms with documented loss of function, exam findings of hip pathology, and a failed course of conservative care, and my records address each of those points as set out above. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed, and every day this is delayed is another day I am limited to one block of walking with a cane.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-09, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; any member who is unsure where to file can call the number on the back of the insurance card and ask where member appeals are filed.

Please confirm in writing that you have received this appeal. I am happy to provide any additional records you need, and I ask that you contact me if anything is missing rather than closing the appeal as incomplete.

Thank you for your time and careful review.

Sincerely,

**Skyler Foster**
Member ID: W944120051
[Signature]
[Date]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-13 (reference POC-DA7FAA7DB4-93242)
- Radiograph report dated 2026-06-08
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-11 to 2026-07-01, 16 visits)
- Office notes from Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery
- [Any other records I am enclosing]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
